title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 663-664): Grothendieck wants to extend a group homomorphism defined over a schematically dense open U of a base S, after replacing it by a 'multiple'. On p. 663 he writes it as G_m -> G with lambda -> phi(lambda^n). This page and the next show that the intended source is G_a with lambda -> phi(m*lambda), corrected explicitly on the next page. As a 'decisive test' he takes G = GL_n and S = Spec A, A a regular local ring of dimension 1 (a DVR) with fraction field K.

In characteristic 0, a homomorphism G_{a,K} -> GL_{n,K} is lambda -> exp(lambda X) with X in M_n(K) nilpotent, so X^n = 0. The hypothesis that phi(1) extends to a section over S reads exp(X) in M_n(A) and exp(-X) in M_n(A); this is (18).

The composite phi o u_d (lambda -> phi(d*lambda)) extends to a homomorphism G_{a,A} -> GL_{n,A} exactly when exp(d*lambda*X) lies in GL_n(A[lambda]). That holds exactly when d^i X^i / i! lies in M_n(A) for 1 <= i <= n-1; this is (19).

Characteristic 0 case (left margin). If A is a Q-algebra, (19) is equivalent to X in M_n(A), so phi itself should extend. Proof: Y := exp(X) - 1 = X + X^2/2! + ... + X^{n-1}/(n-1)! lies in M_n(A) and is nilpotent. Hence X = log(1+Y) = Y - Y^2/2 + Y^3/3 - ... is a finite sum with rational coefficients, so it lies in M_n(A).

Display (20) records the first case n = 5 that he looks at. Its exact content is partly crossed out and hard to read.

Mixed characteristic (residue characteristic p, K of characteristic 0). The same log formula shows that X has only p-power denominators, bounded in terms of n. Indeed Y in M_n(A) and X = sum over k < n of (-1)^{k+1} Y^k/k. Hence p^a X lies in M_n(A) for some a. Since the valuations of i! for i < n are bounded, d = p^nu works in (19). This settles the earlier troublesome case (n = 4, residue characteristic 2) by taking d a large power of 2.

He then states a corollary. Let S have residue characteristic p, and let phi be defined on an open set containing S - V(p), i.e. the complement of U lies in characteristic p; locality of S is unnecessary. Then some q = p^nu makes phi^q (= phi o u_q) extend.

The next page generalises this to a conjectured proposition. For affine G over noetherian S, U = S - V(n) schematically dense, and phi_U : G_a|U -> G|U, there is m = n^r such that phi_U o u_m extends to G_a -> G.
errors: On the previous page the source group is written G_m and the twist lambda -> phi(lambda^n). For the exponential argument on this page the correct setting is G_a with lambda -> phi(n*lambda); Grothendieck fixes this himself on the next page.

The hypothesis exp(-X) in M_n(A) in (18) is redundant. det exp(X) = 1, so the inverse of exp X is its adjugate and already has entries in A. Equivalently, exp(-X) = (1+Y)^{-1} is a polynomial in the nilpotent Y.

Display (20) is partly crossed out; its intended implication is unclear. The sign written '±' in the transcription should be determined from the exponential series. As literally read, 'X^2/2 + X^3/3! + X^4/4! in M_5(A) => X in M_5(A)' is not a correct statement in general without the hypothesis X in M_5(A) or exp X in M_5(A) being specified.

ideas.what: A homomorphism G_a -> GL_n over the generic point of a DVR becomes integral after precomposition with multiplication by a suitable integer d (a power of the residue characteristic), via exp/log with bounded denominators.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of unipotent one-parameter subgroups / integrality of exponentials of nilpotent matrices (truncated exp and log, divided powers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; related to Serre's and Seitz's work on exponentials of unipotent elements and to the theory of integral models / dilatations (Bruhat-Tits, Néron models)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; SGA 3 treats extension of homomorphisms from tori (G_m), not this G_a statement.

ideas.what: In characteristic 0, phi(1) integral implies phi itself extends, because X = log(exp X) is a finite polynomial with rational coefficients.
ideas.modern_name: Exponential/logarithm bijection between nilpotent and unipotent matrices over Q-algebras

ideas.what: Corollary / conjectured proposition: if the complement of U lies over V(p), or V(n), then phi o u_{p^nu} (resp. u_{n^r}) extends to all of S, for any affine group scheme G.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of homomorphisms G_a -> G across a closed set of positive characteristic after Frobenius-free 'scaling' (cf. dilatations of G_a)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; close in spirit to dilatation / Néron blowup techniques (Raynaud, Bosch-Lütkebohmert-Raynaud)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, as a conjecture or lemma, an extension principle for G_a-homomorphisms into affine (or general finitely presented) group schemes over a schematically dense open U: phi o u_m extends for m a power of n whenever S - U lies in V(n). He checks it only for GL_n over a DVR. The general case for affine G, and for general group schemes over normal bases, is left open on these pages.
missed.quote: on suppose que φ_U(1) = g_U se prolonge ... Alors il existe un entier n>0 tel que φ_U^n ... se prolonge ... Je ne vais pas essayer de le démontrer dans ce contexte général
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a clean statement about integral models of unipotent one-parameter subgroups in mixed characteristic. It is relevant to extending G_a-actions and to integral structures in Bruhat-Tits and Néron theory, but it is likely known or easy for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a correct and essentially routine exp/log denominator argument. The general extension statement for G_a-homomorphisms after scaling is a mildly interesting unpublished formulation, but it is likely folklore.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'le cas de car. nulle se résoud par l'affirmative à l'aide de la fonction logarithme, puisque X + X^2/2! + ... + X^{n-1}/(n-1)! = Y, on a exp X = 1+Y, d'où X = log(1+Y) = Y - Y^2/2 + Y^3/3 ...'; the last lines are probably 'Mais en car. mixte ... de base ...'.
'ceci [-implique-] est équivalent d'ailleurs : X ∈ M_n(A)'; the denominator under X is crossed out, so the condition is X ∈ M_n(A).
'Corollaire aux lemmes dessus[?] relatifs' is likely 'Corollaire aux lemmes de relèvement?'; uncertain.
'car. p ≠ 0' should probably read 'car. p > 0'. 'q = p^ν' reads correctly.
